objectives.text: Keep the customs union and the monetary and diplomatic arrangements with Switzerland: the customs union has run since 1924, the franc has been the currency since 1920, and Switzerland represents Liechtenstein abroad unless it chooses otherwise. Without the Swiss tie the state has no army, no foreign service of its own and no market of its own.

objectives.text: Keep full access to the EU single market and to the Schengen area without being an EU member. The EEA has applied since 1 May 1995 and Schengen since December 2011 as an associate member. The EU is not a partner of choice here but the source of most of the rules the state must adopt.

objectives.text: Keep the financial centre''s access to US capital markets while meeting US tax-information and sanctions demands. The 2014 FATCA agreement was signed in Vaduz to protect that access, and in 2025 US pressure pushed fiduciaries to drop Russian-linked trusts.

means.text: The financial centre: a fiduciary and trust sector that manages wealth across borders. In 2025 the sector shrank under US secondary-sanctions pressure, and the state now looks to centralise supervision of trusts it cannot close.

Multilateral presence far above its size: UN, Council of Europe, OSCE, WTO and ICC membership, plus voluntary contributions to Council of Europe action plans, including CHF 115,000 for Ukraine''s recovery plan (signed 13 Nov 2025).

sources.title: Liechtenstein funds Council of Europe action plans and projects

means.text: No army. Policing is done by the national Security Corps, which trains mostly in Switzerland and Austria. Security is delegated in practice to its neighbours, with no air-policing agreement of its own.

constraints.text: No army, and Switzerland says it would not defend Liechtenstein directly because that would break Swiss neutrality (Federal Council, reaffirmed February 2025). The state cannot back its foreign policy with force.

constraints.text: Monetary and customs dependence on Switzerland: the Swiss franc is the currency and Swiss customs law applies at the border. Liechtenstein cannot set its own tariffs or monetary policy, and its trade statistics leave Switzerland out.

constraints.text: Small size and exposure to US secondary sanctions. The trust sector depends on being acceptable to US banks and regulators, so US pressure on Russian clients translates directly into a fiduciary shutdown inside the country.

paradoxes.text: The clean-up that keeps the state in US good standing leaves Russian-linked trusts without managers, so the assets sit frozen instead of being administered. The financial centre earns from the same assets it is now forced to isolate.

grand_strategy.reading:
Liechtenstein has no army and no market of its own, so its strategy is to rent out
its legal and financial order and to borrow its security and currency from Switzerland
and its market access from the EU through the EEA. The vulnerable point is the financial
centre, which must stay acceptable to Washington at the price of shrinking itself: in 2025
US pressure pushed fiduciaries out of Russian-linked trusts. Ukraine support, in money and in
Council of Europe programmes, is how it shows a Western profile without military weight.

stances.note: Customs union in force since 1924 and franc currency since 1920, with Switzerland representing Liechtenstein abroad unless Vaduz chooses otherwise (treaty-based, so the grade is "ally" in the ontology sense). No defence guarantee: the Federal Council reaffirmed in February 2025 that Switzerland would not defend Liechtenstein directly. Bond - affinity: shared language and a shared neutrality tradition; the sources do not describe kinship, so the bond is our reading.

sources.title: Federal Council confirms: Switzerland would not defend Liechtenstein

stances.note: Neighbour with no treaty of alliance and no defence tie. Courts are modelled on Austrian rules and police training runs partly in Austria, but Liechtenstein is left out of the Swiss-Austrian air-policing arrangement. The grade is our reading of a transactional neighbourhood (confidence C): no source uses the word "partner" for this pair. Bond - affinity: shared German-speaking legal and cultural space, not kinship.

The EU is partner for a non-member under the ontology, even though Liechtenstein is inside the EEA (since 1 May 1995) and an associate of Schengen (since December 2011): the EEA is recorded as a treaty row, not as an ally grade. Liechtenstein adopts most EU single-market rules and follows EU sanctions through the EEA. Bond - none: interest-based membership, no sympathy or kinship claimed in the sources.

sources.title: The European Union and the Principality of Liechtenstein

stances.note: Diplomatic relations since 10 Feb 1997 and a 2014 FATCA agreement signed in Vaduz to keep access to US capital markets. Structurally transactional: the state accepts US tax and sanctions demands to keep its financial centre working, and in 2025 US secondary-sanctions pressure pushed fiduciaries out of Russian-linked trusts. Trend stable, not cooling: Vaduz still complies rather than resists. Bond - none: pure interest, nothing underneath. No source uses the word "partner" for this pair; the grade is our reading (confidence C).

sources.title: Liechtenstein signs FATCA agreement with the United States

stances.note: Diplomatic relations since 6 Feb 1992. Support is financial and diplomatic, not military: CHF 8 million for rapid recovery and CHF 800,000 for EBRD capital announced in April 2025 (figures as reported by the Ukrainian government), a Council of Europe contribution of CHF 115,000 signed 13 Nov 2025, and an honorary consulate opened in Vaduz in June 2024. Ukraine\'s foreign minister praised the "consistent backing" in January 2026: that is Kyiv\'s statement, tier 1 for the statement, not for the grade. Warming because the 2025 funding and ministerial contacts are new. Bond - affinity: sympathy for a state under attack, no kinship.
